p: even a meal like that of Shlomo in his time."
a meal like that of Shlomo in his time,
וְלֹא כִּסְעוּדַת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and not like the meal of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him;
for in the Gemara (Bava Metzia 86b) they said:
"Is this to say that the meal of Avraham Avinu
was greater than that of Shlomo?
here, for all of Yisrael and Yehudah,
It appears that from this there is support
that one who is accustomed every Shabbos
to eat the third meal together with companions
on this Shabbos on which falls
תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב אוֹ עֶרֶב תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב גַּם כֵּן
Tishah B'Av or Erev Tishah B'Av as well,
in accordance with the view of the Bechor Shor,
who disagreed with the Magen Avraham
that one should not sit at a meal with companions;
that this is not comparable to what the Rokeach wrote,
that one should sit in anguish of soul,
for that is a private matter,
to eat the third meal with companions
and he brought a proof for this;
And from the fact that the Gemara cited above mentions
which, as is explained in the Gemara (Bava Metzia 86b),
was for all of Yisrael and Yehudah,
that one should not change on this Shabbos
from his custom of eating with companions
every Shabbos at the third meal.
as the sand of the sea,
וּבְכָאן הָא הָרוֹקֵחַ גַּם כֵּן כָּתַב
But here, the Rokeach too wrote
that one should sit in anguish of soul.
that his heart should be in anguish of soul,
וְהִנֵּה בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (אֵיכָה רַבָּה ג, ה) אִיתָא
Now in the Midrash (Eichah Rabbah 3:5) it says:
"'And the songs of the drinkers of strong drink' (Tehillim 69:13):
and become intoxicated at the meal of Tishah B'Av,
that from this there is support
for eating somewhat more at the first meal
but only to the meal with which one concludes before the fast.
"Whatever is of the meal of Tishah B'Av,
it is forbidden to eat meat
we see that it calls "the meal of Tishah B'Av"
the meal with which one concludes.
when he had eaten all his food,
זוֹ הוּא סְעוּדַת תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב וְכוּלֵּי
This is the meal of Tishah B'Av," etc.
And so it is in the Yerushalmi (Taanis 4:6),
and it is mentioned in the Magen Avraham as well.
And in the glosses of the Maharal
about the expression "at the meal of Tishah B'Av,"
to the time of the Second Temple;
they would read then as well
and likewise in the future too
Megillas Eichah will not be abolished,
since it is one of the twenty-four books,
and they are forever and ever;
as is written in the commentators,
who explain the pesukim of Eichah for the good;
and especially in the Pesichta (Eichah Rabbah, Pesichta 17),
and become intoxicated at the meal of Tishah B'Av,
in the time of the Beis HaMikdash,
on "and the songs of the drinkers of strong drink,"
and this is 'and the songs of the drinkers of strong drink'"
to call the cantillation of Eichah
for they are not a melody
but only notes of weeping and eulogy.

p: With what do you sanctify it?
With food and with drink, etc....,
And so it is in the Midrash Rabbah
(Shir HaShirim, end of chapter 5; Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:16).
is it not also written in the Torah
"Observe the Shabbos day to sanctify it,"
"Remember the Shabbos day to sanctify it";
so why did it bring the pasuk from Yechezkel?
But in the Torah it is written "to sanctify it,"
that there should be holiness in it;
they will bring holiness into Shabbos
and it is not stated as a command.
so that there is holiness on Shabbos,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב צב, ב)
where "sanctify" is written as a command,
that they should sanctify Shabbos by an action
whereas all the holiness of Shabbos
"If one sat and did not commit a transgression,
like those who do a mitzvah";
when all Yisrael abstain from work
it is as though a transgression came to his hand
and he was saved from it,
and he is like one who does a mitzvah;
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ עַל זֶה
nevertheless, one cannot apply to this
And on this they said in the Midrash Rabbah:
they also bring holiness into Shabbos,
כָּל שֶׁלֹּא עָבַר כָּל יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת
as long as the whole Shabbos day has not passed,
that Shabbos will pass with proper guarding.
our Sages, of blessed memory, instituted
at night and in the morning,
except in the place of a meal;
is of the aspect of the "preserved wine,"
This is not so at the third meal:
since the whole Shabbos day has already passed
our Sages, of blessed memory, did not institute
making Kiddush over wine at this meal,
עַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת מִמְּלָאכָה לְבַד
through guarding Shabbos from work alone,
which is like doing a mitzvah,
they have already brought holiness into Shabbos,
"Observe the Shabbos day to sanctify it,"
And as for the practice of the holy Arizal
to drink wine during the meal
"and wine to those bitter of soul";
"And wine gladdens the heart of man — enosh,"
that is, even one who is
"Fortunate is the man — enosh — who does this":
and the days of work arrive,
then a person is very bitter of soul;
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
may the memory of the tzaddik and holy one be for a blessing for the life of the World to Come,
who said in the name of someone
it is as though he is cast
And for this reason we say
I will trust and not be afraid";
and one does not say "do not fear"
except to one who is afraid;
for then fear falls upon a person
when he sees that he is leaving
I will trust and not be afraid."
And because of this we also say
to bring joy to those bitter of soul.
Therefore, on a Shabbos on which falls
תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב אוֹ עֶרֶב תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב
Tishah B'Av or Erev Tishah B'Av,
the heart must be in sadness
and for this the wine is needed
And this is what they said in the Gemara cited above:
even a meal like that of Shlomo in his time,"

p: "Bring us back, Hashem, to You, and we shall return;
renew our days as of old;
for You have utterly rejected us," etc.
We must understand what this is:
a reason given for what precedes it?
since they are among the books of the Kesuvim;
yet we have already spoken above
at a time of lamentation and destruction.
However, one may say in this
according to what was written by
on what they said in the Gemara there:
"A sage is greater than a prophet"
and through this he can apprehend
And one can apply to this
the statement of Chazal (end of Makkos; 24b)
who were going up to Yerushalayim, etc.:
that came out of the Kodesh HaKodashim;
it is certain that the prophecy of Zechariah
In these words they said to him:
and not believe all the promises
about the consolations of the time to come,
on "a sage is greater than a prophet,"
and according to their statement, of blessed memory
"And his eye saw every precious thing":
"Things that were not revealed to Moshe
were revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues."
of the wisdom of Torah she'b'al peh
in the writings of the Arizal),
Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
which was of the aspect of prophecy
more than Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yehoshua.
And this is why they said to him
for specifically through his aspect and his power
there shone forth in them too
of why Yirmiyahu concludes the lamentations,
which were said with ruach hakodesh,
"Bring us back, Hashem, to You, and we shall return;
renew our days as of old"
when the corruption did not yet exist.
You have been very angry with us";
and surely this is the cause
through which there will be renewed
that there was never any mourning at all;
"And I will turn their mourning into gladness,
and make them rejoice from their sorrow"
